workflows.name: Qualify website leads with Claude, GoHighLevel, Slack and Gmail

user.name: Kingsley Ken
user.bio: Kingsley Ken is a verified n8n creator and AI automation builder specialising in n8n workflow automation for agencies, e-commerce brands and sales teams. He builds AI-driven workflows with built-in accuracy checks and approval steps, so businesses can automate repetitive work without losing control of what goes out. He helps companies in the US, UK, Canada, Europe and Australia replace manual processes with reliable n8n automation.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives website form enquiries via a webhook, qualifies them with Anthropic Claude using quote-verified evidence, saves the lead to GoHighLevel and an n8n Data Table, then requests approval in Slack before sending an email reply through Gmail.

How it works
Receives a website enquiry via a webhook and normalizes fields, generates a fingerprint, and rejects submissions with an invalid email or too-short message.
Loads your business rules and IDs, validates that required settings are filled, and checks an n8n Data Table to skip enquiries that were already processed.
Uses Anthropic Claude to evaluate the enquiry against your qualification rules and then verifies that any quoted evidence actually appears in the enquiry text.
Creates or updates the contact in GoHighLevel, creates an opportunity in the configured pipeline stage, and adds a note containing the qualification assessment.
Uses Anthropic Claude to draft a short plain-text reply based on the qualification outcome and stores the draft and lead metadata in an n8n Data Table.
Sends the enquiry details, checks, and draft to a Slack user for approval, where they choose to send as-is, send with edits, or decline.
If approved, sends the reply via Gmail, updates the Data Table status to sent, and moves the GoHighLevel opportunity to the contacted stage; if declined, marks the Data Table record as not sent.

Setup
Create an n8n Data Table with the columns used by the workflow (fingerprint, email, name, fit, summary, draft, status, contact_id, opportunity_id, decision) and paste its table ID into the client settings.
Create a GoHighLevel Private Integration token with access to contacts and opportunities, then fill in your GoHighLevel location ID, pipeline ID, and the stage IDs for new leads and contacted leads.
Add credentials for Anthropic (Claude), Slack OAuth2, Gmail, and an HTTP Bearer Auth credential for the GoHighLevel HTTP requests.
Update the values in the client settings (business details, rules, reply instructions, and the Slack approver member ID).
Copy the production webhook URL and configure your website form to POST name, email, phone, and message to it.

Requirements
A GoHighLevel sub-account with API access, Slack, Gmail, an Anthropic API key and n8n data tables.

Customization
Edit the rules, the not a fit description and the reply instructions in Set Client Settings to suit any service business. The GoHighLevel nodes can be swapped for another CRM, and Gmail for another email node.

workflows.name: Reply to web form leads instantly with Resend, Slack and n8n forms
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow captures inbound web-form leads via an n8n Form, an authenticated webhook, or a manual test run, screens out spam/duplicates, logs every submission to an n8n Data Table, and notifies you via Resend email and optional Slack, including an instant acknowledgement to accepted leads.

How it works
Triggers when a lead is submitted through the n8n Form, posted to the webhook endpoint, or started via a manual test run.
Validates the configuration and, for webhook requests, checks the x-leads-key header against your shared secret.
Normalizes incoming payloads from common form formats (Typeform, Tally, Google Forms, Webflow, or plain JSON) into a consistent lead schema.
Screens each lead for honeypots, invalid/blocked email domains, spam keywords, too-short messages, too many links, duplicates within a time window, and hourly rate limits.
Creates (if needed) and upserts every lead—accepted or rejected—into an n8n Data Table with status and spam/duplicate reasons.
For accepted leads only, sends an owner alert via Resend email and optionally posts an alert to Slack via an incoming webhook.
Optionally sends the lead a Resend acknowledgement email (or routes it to the owner in sample mode) while continuing the workflow even if any notification fails.

Setup
Add a Resend API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential (Bearer token) and select it in both Resend HTTP Request steps.
In the Config values, set businessName, ownerEmail, and emailFrom (must be on a verified Resend domain), and decide whether to enable sendLeadAck.
If using the webhook trigger, set a strong webhookKey in Config and configure your form tool to POST to the webhook URL with the x-leads-key header.
If you want Slack alerts, create a Slack incoming webhook URL and paste it into slackWebhookUrl, then include slack in alertChannels.
Review and adjust anti-spam settings like spamKeywords, blockedEmailDomains, dedupeHours, and maxLeadsPerHour, and turn off sampleData before going live.

Additional info
This is a free slice of the full Inbound Lead Responder kit by VNCNT Labs. Get the complete kit: https://vncntlabs.gumroad.com/l/inbound-lead-responder?utm_source=n8n&utm_campaign=speed-to-lead

workflows.name: Score B2B leads and draft cold emails with Google Sheets, Apify and OpenAI

user.name: Kseniia
user.bio: Software engineer building B2B data enrichment and workflow automation tools.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every 30 minutes (or manually) to pull B2B leads from Google Sheets, enrich them via Apify (domain/tech/MX, hiring signals, and Google Ads activity), score fit and intent, and use OpenAI to draft outreach emails that are saved as Gmail drafts and synced back to Sheets.

How it works
Runs on a 30-minute schedule (or manual trigger), loads the sender/ICP configuration, and reads lead rows from Google Sheets.
Selects a batch of new or stale leads (30-day TTL) and retryable items (up to the max retry count), then locks them by setting Status to Processing in Google Sheets.
Calls the Apify Company Domain Finder, Tech Stack & MX/DNS Enricher (https://apify.com/xenikii/company-domain-tech-stack-enricher) and separates accounts into Verified + MX, No MX (LinkedIn / Call Only), Needs Review (Low Confidence), Needs Review / Retry (bounded retry count), and Unresolved Domain.
For verified domains with MX, queries Apify B2B Hiring Signals & Multi-ATS Job Scraper (https://apify.com/xenikii/company-career-ats-job-scraper) and Google Ads Transparency Scraper (https://apify.com/xenikii/google-ads-transparency-scraper) in parallel (with alwaysOutputData and automatic retry handling on transient errors).
Computes Fit_Score (0–50), Intent_Score (0–50), Total_Score (0–100: Hot >= 75, Warm 55–74, Cold = 55) in target geographies, uses OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) to generate a grounded, language-matched 3-sentence cold email draft with a code-enforced GDPR opt-out footer.
Creates a Gmail draft for leads with a valid primary email and syncs the final scores, enrichment data, and draft status back to Google Sheets.

Setup
Create a Google Sheet with columns: Company, Country, Status, Retry_Count, Outreach_Status, Resolved_Name, Domain, Website, Fit_Score, Intent_Score, Total_Score, Intent_Tier, Score_Breakdown, Outreach_Channel, Email_Provider, DMARC_Policy, Tech_Stack, ATS_Provider, Open_Jobs, New_Jobs_30d, Hiring_Focus, Sample_Roles, Active_Google_Ads, Evergreen_Ads, Primary_Email, Role_Emails, Phones, LinkedIn_URL, Description, AI_Email_Subject, AI_Email_Body, Last_Enriched_At.
Add an Apify API token using HTTP Header Auth (Authorization: Bearer ) for the three Apify HTTP requests.
Add an OpenAI credential and confirm the selected model (gpt-4o-mini) is available in your OpenAI account.
Add a Gmail OAuth2 credential for creating drafts and ensure the Google Sheet document and sheet names/IDs point to your own spreadsheet.
Open the Sender & ICP Config node to set your senderName (must be changed from YOUR_NAME_AND_COMPANY to enable Gmail draft creation), offerSummary, callToAction, targetCountries, and targetTechKeywords before activating the schedule.

Requirements
Google Sheets OAuth2, Gmail OAuth2, OpenAI API key, and Apify API token (HTTP Header Auth: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN).

Customization
Adjust batchSize (default 10 rows per 30 min = 480 leads/day), warmScoreThreshold (55), hotScoreThreshold (75), targetCountries, and targetTechKeywords in the Sender & ICP Config node.

Additional info
Uses three Apify intelligence signals: Company Domain Finder, Tech Stack & MX/DNS Enricher (https://apify.com/xenikii/company-domain-tech-stack-enricher), B2B Hiring Signals & Multi-ATS Job Scraper (https://apify.com/xenikii/company-career-ats-job-scraper), and Google Ads Transparency Scraper (https://apify.com/xenikii/google-ads-transparency-scraper).

workflows.name: Score Google Maps review-based leads with Apify, Groq and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow manually runs an Apify Google Maps scrape for businesses and their lowest-rated reviews, uses Groq to extract complaint-based pain points and a fit score for your service, and upserts the resulting leads (with evidence quotes and an opener) into Google Sheets.

How it works
Starts when you manually execute the workflow.
Loads your search parameters (query, location, volumes, service description, and minimum fit score) and reads existing leads from Google Sheets to avoid reprocessing.
Calls Apify’s Google Places crawler to fetch businesses and their lowest-ranked reviews for the configured search term and location, stopping with an error if scraping fails.
Bundles each business’s listing details and review text, then keeps only businesses that are new (not already in the sheet) and have usable review text.
Processes businesses one at a time and sends the review bundle to Groq to return structured JSON with pain points, an evidence quote, a 1–10 fit score, and an outreach opener when the score is high enough.
Formats each result into a lead record with a status (qualified, low_fit, or analysis_failed) and upserts it into the Google Sheets Leads tab by place_id.
Waits the configured number of seconds between AI calls to respect rate limits, then continues with the next business.

Setup
Create a Google Sheet with a tab named “Leads” and columns matching the workflow’s output (including place_id as the unique key), then select the spreadsheet in both Google Sheets nodes.
Add Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials in n8n.
Add an Apify API token as an HTTP Bearer Auth credential and ensure your Apify account has enough credits to run the compass/crawler-google-places actor.
Add a Groq API key credential and optionally adjust the selected model.
Update the “Search settings” values (search term, location, business/review limits, your service description, minimum fit score, review language, and seconds between AI calls) before running.

workflows.name: Reply to web form leads via Gmail or Quo and log them in Google Sheets

user.name: Nathan
user.bio:
I build n8n workflows for owner-run service businesses that lose jobs when a call goes to voicemail or a web form sits unread.
My paid template, Lead Catch, gives every missed-call and web form lead an instant reply and a follow-up three days later, all logged in one Google Sheet.
It is built for US businesses texting through Quo and comes with a setup guide. Get it at the link below.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Service businesses with a website form and a Quo (formerly OpenPhone) number, who want every lead answered fast and texted only with consent.

How it works
Your form posts each lead here.
A lead with an email gets a Gmail reply.
A phone-only lead gets a Quo text only when the form's consent box was ticked and the number never opted out.
Anyone else gets no reply, and the reason goes on their row so you call them back.
Every lead becomes a row in a Leads sheet. A repeat inside 24 hours adds a note, not a second row or reply.
Gmail tells you who it was and what reply went out.

Setup
Make a Google Sheet with a tab named Leads and these headers in row 1: received_at, source, name, phone, email, message, status, reply_sent_at, reply_channel, followup_sent_at, do_not_text, notes. Set the phone column to Plain text.
Add Google Sheets credentials to the three Sheets nodes and Gmail to the two Gmail nodes.
In the Quo text node, add a Header Auth credential: name Authorization, value your Quo API key.
Fill in Settings: sheet ID, your email, business name and phone, Quo number, timezone. Check the reply texts.
Add a checkbox named sms_consent to your form, by the phone field, unticked, with this line: By entering your phone number, you agree to get texts from (your business) about your request: a reply and at most one follow-up. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.
Activate, then point your form at the Production URL.

Requirements
Quo with US carrier registration, Google and n8n.

Customization
Edit the reply texts and the repeat window in Settings.

workflows.name: Verify scraped lead emails with Apify and Google Sheets

user.name: Edge
user.bio: I build n8n workflows that find and qualify local-business leads with official APIs. Free templates here; the full Lead List Builder is on my Gumroad.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs manually or on a weekly schedule to verify scraped lead emails using Apify’s Bulk Email Verifier, sourcing leads from either a Google Sheet or an Apify dataset, and then writes verification results back to Google Sheets or splits them into new Apify datasets by verdict.

How it works
Runs manually or every Monday at 08:00.
Checks the Settings to decide whether to process an Apify dataset ID or read leads from a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
When using Google Sheets, reads rows where the email status is empty or set to “unknown”, extracts email addresses from the email column, and batches them up to the configured limits.
Runs the Apify “Bulk Email Verifier: syntax, MX, disposable, role and typo” Actor to verify the emails and retrieve the results dataset.
If the input came from Google Sheets, matches verification results back to each sheet row and updates the sheet with “Email status”, “Best email”, and “Email notes”.
If the input came from an Apify dataset, groups results by verdict (valid/risky/invalid/unknown), creates a new Apify dataset per verdict, and uploads the corresponding rows.

Setup
Install the community node package @apify/n8n-nodes-apify in your n8n instance.
Create an Apify API credential in n8n and select it for the Apify Actor node and the Apify HTTP Request nodes.
If using Google Sheets as the source, add a Google Sheets OAuth credential, set the document ID and sheet name in both Google Sheets nodes, and ensure your sheet has columns matching the configured email and status headers (for example “Email” and “Email status”).
If using an Apify dataset as the source, paste the dataset ID (or dataset URL) into apifyDatasetId in Settings and confirm the correct emailField name for items in that dataset.
Review the Settings values (for example maxEmails, batchSize, timeoutSeconds, and optional checkSmtp) to fit your volume and verification strictness before activating the schedule.

Requirements
n8n with the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify (tested with version 0.9.0 on n8n 2.45.5). Install guide: https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/
An Apify account and its API token (Apify Console, Settings, Integrations)
Google Sheets access, only for the sheet route

Customization
Raise maxEmails or batchSize in Settings to check more addresses per execution
Turn on checkSmtp to also probe the mailbox (slower, and many mail servers block the probe)
Change resultDatasetPrefix to name the new result datasets your way

Additional info
Cost: the Bulk Email Verifier Actor is pay per event on Apify: $0.0006 per address with a verdict (valid, risky or invalid), free for status unknown, plus $0.00005 per run start (prices read 6 Nov 2026). Valid means the domain accepts mail; the mailbox itself is probed only with checkSmtp on. Actor page: https://apify.com/edgef-4/bulk-email-verifier

workflows.name: Text new form leads instantly via iMessage and SMS with iBlueText
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects new leads via an n8n form, formats and validates their phone numbers, sends an iMessage or SMS via iBlueText, and checks delivery status after a short delay to surface send or delivery failures.

How it works
Receives a new lead submission from an n8n Form with the lead’s name, mobile number, and request details.
Builds the outbound message and normalizes the submitted phone number into international E.164 format.
Skips the lead if the phone number does not pass validation.
Sends the text message through the iBlueText API using an HTTP request with header-based authentication.
Waits one minute and then queries iBlueText for the send status using the returned message ID.
Stops with an error if iBlueText reports a failed delivery, otherwise finishes successfully.

Setup
Create an iBlueText account and generate an API key (or use a sandbox test key for testing).
In n8n, add an HTTP Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer  and select it for both iBlueText HTTP requests.
Customize the default country code and message text in the workflow settings, and ensure your trigger provides a first name and phone number if you replace the built-in form.
Activate the workflow and share the n8n Form URL (or configure your external lead source to send data to the trigger you use).

Requirements
An iBlueText account (free to start) and an API key from Integrations → API keys. Sandbox test keys (sk-ibt-test-) let you test without texting anyone.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives inbound leads via a webhook, normalizes the submitted fields, uses OpenAI to score and categorize each lead, appends the results to Google Sheets, and posts a Slack alert for hot leads before responding to the webhook caller with the lead tier.

How it works
Receives a POST request on a webhook containing lead details from a form or website.
Normalizes the incoming payload into consistent name, email, company, and message fields.
Sends the normalized lead text to OpenAI and parses the model response into structured JSON containing score, tier, reason, and next step.
Combines the original lead fields with the AI scoring results into a single record.
Appends the lead record to a Google Sheets worksheet.
Checks whether the lead score meets the hot-lead threshold (>= 70) and posts a formatted alert to a Slack channel when it does.
Returns a JSON webhook response indicating the lead was received and includes the computed tier.

Setup
Add credentials for OpenAI, Google Sheets (OAuth2), and Slack.
Create a Google Sheet with a “Leads” tab and columns: Date, Name, Email, Company, Message, Score, Tier, Reason, Next Step.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in the Google Sheets append step and confirm the target sheet name matches your document.
Set the Slack channel (for example #sales-leads) where hot-lead alerts should be posted.
Copy the webhook URL and configure your form tool or website to send a POST payload with fields like name/full_name, email, company, and message/details.

user.bio:
I build n8n and HubSpot automations that keep running when something fails: AI call reports, lead routing and CRM cleanup, with retries, clear error paths and grouped failure alerts built in.
I run automations like these in production every day. Fixed price per build, async from Georgia (GMT+4): chargegrove.com

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives website form leads via a webhook, uses OpenAI to classify intent and urgency, scores and routes each lead with custom rules, and then creates or updates the contact in HubSpot while optionally creating a follow-up task for qualified leads.

How it works
Receives a new lead submission via a POST webhook.
Validates and pre-screens the lead details (especially email domain and message content) to flag spam, disposable emails, and other risk signals.
Searches HubSpot for an existing contact by email to preserve the current owner when a match is found.
Sends the lead details and message to OpenAI Chat Completions to return a JSON classification for intent, urgency, and a short summary.
Combines the checks, HubSpot lookup result, and AI output to calculate a score from 0 to 100, assign a tier (A/B/C or rejected), pick a route, and select an owner ID.
Stops and returns a “rejected” webhook response for spam/job/disposable or invalid leads, otherwise upserts the contact in HubSpot with scoring fields and notes.
Creates a HubSpot task for tier A and B leads with an appropriate due time (A in 1 hour, B tomorrow) and returns a “routed” webhook response with the scoring details.

Setup
Create a HubSpot private app with contacts read and write scopes, add its token as a HubSpot App Token credential, and select it on every HubSpot HTTP Request node.
Add an OpenAI credential and select it on the "AI: read the message" node.
Create the HubSpot contact properties used by the workflow (lead_fit_score, lead_tier, lead_route, lead_intent, lead_check_notes, ai_lead_summary). The main sticky note lists each type and its dropdown options.
Replace the placeholder HubSpot owner IDs in the Config node (owner_enterprise, owner_smb, owner_support) with real numeric owner IDs. Left as placeholders or blank, new contacts and tasks are created without an owner.
Activate the workflow, copy the production webhook URL (path /new-lead), and have your form POST firstname, lastname, email, company, website, jobtitle, company_size, country, budget and message.

Requirements
HubSpot account (the free CRM works) with a private app token
OpenAI API key

Customization
Points, thresholds and routes: the "Score and route" Code node
Free and disposable email lists: the "Check the lead" Code node
Swap the webhook for a HubSpot, Typeform or Tally trigger, and map the fields to the same names in "Check the lead"

Additional info
Limitations: writes contacts and tasks only, no companies or deals. The score comes from fixed rules; AI only reads intent and urgency. The free (11) and disposable (8) email domain lists are starter lists, so extend them.

Testing: run on n8n 2.1.5 with 5 sample leads against a demo HubSpot account, including the rejected path. The AI step ran through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint set in Config (openai_base_url), so results with the default gpt-4.1-mini may differ slightly.

Synthetic test payload:
{"firstname":"Helena","lastname":"Kovac","email":"helena@example.com","company":"Example Clinics","website":"https://example.com","jobtitle":"VP Operations","company_size":"450","country":"Germany","budget":"25000","message":"Our leads from Google Ads sit in HubSpot for days before anyone calls. Can we talk this week?"}

workflows.name: Qualify Gmail leads and draft replies with OpenAI and HubSpot
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors a Gmail inbox, uses OpenAI to classify and summarize incoming emails, drafts sales replies in Gmail, and creates or updates HubSpot contacts and deals for qualified new leads while sending you notification emails for new leads, replies, and items needing manual review.

How it works
Triggers every minute when a new message arrives in the Gmail inbox (excluding promotions, social, and forums).
Skips emails already processed in previous executions, filters out newsletters/auto-replies and your own messages, and extracts a cleaned plain-text body and customer email.
Sends the email content to OpenAI to classify it as a new lead, a customer reply, or other, and returns a structured summary and confidence score.
Routes the email based on classification confidence and basic safety checks (for example, avoiding replies/forwards and requiring a customer email address).
For qualified new leads, uses OpenAI to write a reply, saves it as a Gmail draft in the same thread, upserts the contact in HubSpot, creates a HubSpot deal, and emails you a notification with the outcome.
For customer replies from known HubSpot contacts (excluding UNQUALIFIED), updates the HubSpot lead status to CONNECTED and emails you a notification.
For anything ambiguous or missing key data, emails you an alert indicating the message needs manual review and does not create a draft or HubSpot record.

Setup
Connect Gmail OAuth2 credentials for the Gmail trigger and all Gmail actions (draft creation and notification emails).
Create and add a HubSpot App Token credential with permission to read and write contacts and deals.
Add an OpenAI API credential for the OpenAI chat model used for classification and reply drafting, and select a model you have access to.
Replace all placeholder values in “Your business details” (company info, notify email, ownEmails, and optional signature, deal stage, and confidence threshold).
If you receive web form emails from a form service address, add those sender addresses to the formSenders list so the workflow can extract the real customer email.

Receives a new lead submission from an n8n Form with name, work email, and an E.164 phone number.

Uses ProWebLook to verify the email’s deliverability status.

Posts the verified lead summary to a selected Slack channel.

Create and select a ProWebLook API credential for the email verification and WhatsApp check steps.
Create a Slack credential, then set the target Slack channel in the Slack message node.
If you embed the n8n Form in another site or tool, copy the form URL and link it from your signup flow.

Requirements
ProWebLook account with API key (50 free Email, Phone & WhatsApp credits included on signup at proweblook.com)

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday morning to scan Gmail for recent threads where someone emailed you but you haven’t replied or drafted a response, then uses OpenAI to prioritize and summarize the most important leads and delivers a single digest to you as a Gmail draft or email.

How it works
Runs every weekday at 8 AM (or manually) and loads configuration like your email, business description, lookback window, and delivery mode.
In test mode it uses a built-in sample inbox, otherwise it fetches recent Gmail messages from your inbox plus your Sent mail and Drafts for the configured lookback period.
Compares incoming threads against your Sent and Draft messages to keep only threads where the newest message is from someone else and you have not replied or started a draft.
Screens the remaining messages to skip newsletters, no-reply/automated senders, and very recent emails, and flags potentially risky or prompt-injection content (for example wire transfer keywords) to keep it out of OpenAI.
Sends the safe candidates to OpenAI with structured output to classify the email type, rate urgency, and generate a short summary and next-step suggestion.
Validates and cleans the AI results, builds a ranked digest with Gmail thread links plus a separate “read these yourself” list for flagged/unclear items, and then either emails the digest to you or saves it as a Gmail draft (and can optionally send even when empty).

Setup
Connect your Gmail account (OAuth2) so the workflow can read your inbox and create a draft or send an email.
Add an OpenAI API credential for the OpenAI Chat Model used by the workflow.
In the configuration step, set your_email and your_business, and optionally adjust lookback_days, quiet_hours, max_ai_checks, tripwires, skip_senders, delivery (draft/email), and send_when_empty.
Run once with test_mode set to yes to verify the digest output using sample emails, then set test_mode to no and activate the scheduled workflow.

workflows.name: Rank remote job leads from six boards with Apify, OpenAI and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow runs daily to pull remote job listings from multiple boards via an Apify actor, deduplicates and scores them with OpenAI, stores results in Google Sheets, and sends hot jobs to Slack for approval and warm jobs to Gmail, with a weekly email report.

How it works
Runs on a daily schedule (or manually), loads configuration values, and decides whether to run the Apify collection or generate the weekly report.
For the daily run, starts the Apify Remote Jobs Aggregator actor, then waits and polls the Apify API until the run succeeds or fails.
Downloads the Apify dataset items, validates required fields, and deduplicates jobs against the current run and a rolling history stored in workflow static data.
Scores each job using rule-based criteria (keywords, seniority, regions, salary, freshness), then uses OpenAI to produce a structured fit score, verdict, summary, outreach angle, and red flags.
Blends the rule score with the OpenAI score to set a final tier (hot/warm/cold) and upserts each job into Google Sheets using the job key to avoid duplicates.
Posts hot jobs to Slack as a single approval message and, based on the response, writes approved/dismissed status back to the same Google Sheets rows.
Emails a daily HTML digest of warm jobs via Gmail, while cold jobs remain available in Google Sheets only.
On Mondays, reads the last 7 days of rows from Google Sheets and emails a weekly summary report via Gmail, and posts any workflow failures to Slack via an error-triggered alert.

Setup
Create an Apify API token and add an HTTP Header Auth credential (Authorization: Bearer ) for the Apify HTTP requests.
Connect Google Sheets credentials, create a spreadsheet tab with the expected columns, and set the Google Sheet ID and tab name in the Config step.
Connect an OpenAI credential (or replace the chat model node with another provider) and ensure the model selection matches your account access.
Connect Slack credentials, set your target channel ID in Config, and update the Slack channel ID used by the error alert step.
Connect Gmail credentials and set the digest recipient email address in Config.
Adjust the Apify actor input, scoring thresholds, keywords, regions, salary minimum, and AI criteria in Config to match your job search preferences.

workflows.name: Find new Swiss B2B leads from SHAB using Apify, Google Sheets and Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick Overview
This workflow runs every weekday morning, pulls newly published Swiss commercial register (SHAB HR01) company entries via an Apify actor, filters them into qualified leads, stores only unseen companies in Google Sheets, and emails a daily HTML summary through Gmail.

How it works
Runs every weekday at 07:00 on a schedule.
Sends a request to an Apify actor to fetch recent SHAB HR01 “new companies” notices for the configured cantons and lookback window.
Filters the results to the allowed legal forms and applies include/exclude keyword matching against the company name and purpose.
Reads existing leads from Google Sheets and removes any companies whose UID is already present to avoid duplicates.
Appends the remaining new companies to the Google Sheets “Leads” tab.
Builds an HTML email containing a table of the new companies and sends it to the configured recipient via Gmail.
If the Apify request fails, sends a failure alert email via Gmail instead of silently producing no results.

Setup
Create an Apify account, add an HTTP Header Auth credential in n8n with Authorization: Bearer , and select it on the Apify HTTP request step.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials and create a spreadsheet with a Leads tab and columns for at least: uid, name, legal_form, seat, canton, address, purpose, matched_keywords, published, shab_url.
Update the configuration values for cantons, legal form codes, keyword filters, lookbackDays/maxItems, and set your Google Sheets URL, tab name, and notification email.
Connect Gmail OAuth credentials for sending the summary and failure-alert emails, then run the workflow once to verify rows append correctly and the email formatting looks right.

workflows.name: Monitor Reddit and score leads with Apify, OpenAI, OpenRouter and Slack
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors Reddit hourly via Apify, filters and scores new posts (with OpenAI/OpenRouter or keyword rules), logs them to an n8n Data Table (optionally Google Sheets), sends high-relevance alerts to Slack, and posts a daily 24-hour digest to Slack every morning.

How it works
Runs on a schedule every hour to fetch newly published Reddit posts from configured subreddits and keyword searches using Apify.
Cleans the results by excluding NSFW content, blocked words, low-score posts, and (optionally) search hits that don’t strictly match your keywords.
Skips posts that have already been processed in previous executions.
Scores each post for relevance and intent and generates a short summary and suggested reply using OpenAI/OpenRouter (or applies a keyword-based scoring fallback when AI is disabled).
Logs each scored post to an n8n Data Table and optionally appends the same data to a Google Sheets tab.
Sends an immediate Slack alert for posts whose relevance meets or exceeds the configured alert threshold.
Runs every morning to compile the last 24 hours of logged posts, optionally uses OpenAI/OpenRouter to write a brief Slack-formatted briefing, and posts the digest to Slack.

Setup
Add an Apify API token credential and ensure the Apify actor run limit (maxSpendUsdPerRun) matches your budget.
Add a Slack OAuth credential, invite the bot to your target channel, and set the channel in both Slack messages (alert and digest).
Add an OpenAI credential (or an OpenRouter key via the same credential by setting the Base URL to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1) if useAI is enabled.
Update the Config values for subreddits, keywords, excluded words, and your “about you” description, plus thresholds like alertScore and digestTopN.
(Optional) Enable the Google Sheets step, connect Google Sheets OAuth, and replace the placeholder document URL and sheet name to log posts to a spreadsheet.

workflows.name: Log trade show exhibitor leads to Google Sheets with Apify and Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs weekly to scrape trade show exhibitor listings with Apify, save and update leads in Google Sheets, and email a digest of new or changed exhibitors via Gmail.

How it works
Runs on a manual start or every Monday at 08:00 (UTC) on a schedule.
Sends your configured show list and filters to the Apify Exhibitor List Scraper actor and waits for the run to finish.
Validates that the Apify actor run succeeded and stops with an error if it fails.
Downloads the actor dataset results from Apify and reads existing rows from the target Google Sheets tab.
Builds a de-duplicated lead list, tags each exhibitor as Ready to contact / Needs research / No contact path, and marks whether each lead is new compared to the sheet.
Appends new leads and updates existing ones in Google Sheets using a generated leadKey match.
Creates an HTML email digest (baseline on first run, otherwise new/updated highlights) and sends it to the configured recipient with Gmail.

Setup
Install the Apify community node and add an Apify API token credential.
Add Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials, create a spreadsheet with a "Leads" sheet (or change the sheet name), and set the spreadsheet ID in the configuration.
Add Gmail OAuth2 credentials and set the recipient email address for the digest.
Edit the configuration to choose the target shows (or start URLs) and any filters (search query, categories, countries), and adjust maxItems and watchlistName as needed.
